yushin-marshal--queen-sunduk.scene: INTRODUCING KIM YUSHIN, thirty-seven, Gaya blood and Silla rank, master of the Hwarang yard. Coronation morning in the palace at Seorabeol: he has stayed at the door of the princess's dressing chamber like a guard. MEDIUM CLOSE-UP from the chest up, low three-quarter angle from her seat: he has dropped to one knee on the threshold and presses his right fist flat against his chest armour over his heart, head slightly bowed, eyes lifted past the camera, steady and warm: "Hwarang Kim Yushin. I will serve you to the end." A level, serious bearded face under hard brows, the rare dry half-smile just starting at one corner of the mouth. Framed above the waist: no sword, no hilt and no weapon anywhere in frame. Cold pre-dawn blue light (#2A5FB8) pours through a paper lattice door at his side and rakes across his face, beard, fist and armour plates. Behind him the corridor dissolves into incense smoke and morning haze: red lacquered pillars, a hanging silk curtain, the warm gold bokeh of coronation lanterns. At the near frame edge, out of focus, the crimson silk sleeve of the princess.

chunchu-prince--queen-sunduk.scene: INTRODUCING KIM CHUNCHU, twenty-nine, already the most cunning man in Samhan — only the quiet rooms know it yet. Coronation morning on the palace road climbing above Seorabeol, on horseback. Low three-quarter angle from beside the horse's shoulder: he rides one-handed with the reins loose, leaning down toward his little daughter seated in front of him in the saddle (only the top of a small child's dark head with a gold hairpin, out of focus at the bottom frame edge), his free hand lifting in a lazy explaining gesture: "You'll bite your tongue." Half-lidded amused eyes, a small knowing smile caught halfway into a laugh at his own joke. A low gold sunrise rakes across his face from the side and sets his magenta-crimson silk burning #D8258C where it catches the light. Behind him, painted loosely in morning haze: the hill road, the tiled roofs of the city far below, coronation banners snapping in the wind, the warm bokeh of lanterns.

gotaso--queen-sunduk.scene: INTRODUCING GOTASO, Chunchu's daughter — whatever it is, she wants it faster. Coronation morning on the palace road above Seorabeol. She is a LITTLE GIRL OF SEVEN, a small child: the sheet's face and hairpin made young and round-cheeked, a child's body. She sits in front of her father on his tall horse. Low angle from the road beside the horse's neck: she leans far forward over the mane, both small fists knotted in it, heels kicking, face bright and fierce with impatience, mouth wide open mid-shout: "Faster! Father. Faster." Of her father only one out-of-focus magenta silk sleeve and hand on the reins at the frame edge. A low pink-gold sunrise (#F0A3C0) rakes across her face and the horse's mane from the side. Behind her, painted loosely in dawn haze and road dust: the hill road climbing, the city's tiled roofs far below, coronation banners whipping in the wind, a bright streaked dawn sky.

munmu-child--queen-sunduk.scene: INTRODUCING BUPMIN, six years old and already drafting laws for the people with no bones. Coronation morning, on his own pony, reined in at the top of the hill road above Seorabeol. He is a TINY BOY OF SIX, a little child: chubby round cheeks, big eyes, short legs that barely reach the stirrups, small hands, the sheet's face design made younger; no beard, no moustache; the sheet's plain blue child's jacket and cream sash; no crown. Low three-quarter angle from the road beside the pony's shoulder: he sits bolt upright in the saddle, arms folded tight across his small chest, chin up, eyes turned DOWN toward the city below with a little king's solemn frown, announcing: "When I'm king everyone has to listen to me." A low sunrise rakes across his face from the side in warm gold light; long plain crimson (#C41E3A) silk streamers on poles snap in the wind beside him — bare cloth, no emblem, no animal, no crown device. Behind and below him, painted loosely in morning haze: the grey tiled roofs of the city, tiny dissolving figures sweeping the long coronation road, a bright dawn sky with wind-streaked cloud.

sunduk-queen--queen-sunduk.scene: INTRODUCING QUEEN SUNDUK, the first Queen of Silla, the Blue Moon of the Divine Country, at the moment she is crowned. The Throne Hall at Seorabeol on coronation morning. Low three-quarter angle from below the dais: she sits upright on the throne, chin level, as two old out-of-focus hands in wide Silla court sleeves lower the gold tree-and-antler crown onto her coiled hair from above the frame; its jade gogok and gold spangles swing and catch the light. Her face is composed and very still, dark eyes forward, a held breath, the faintest private smile of relief pressed into her lips. A low shaft of morning sun through the open hall doors rakes across her face and the phoenix brocade from the side in warm vermilion-gold (#E8552B), striking sparks off the gold. Behind her the hall dissolves into drifting incense smoke: red lacquered pillars, a dim painted screen, the soft gold bokeh of hanging lamps and dust turning in the shaft.

kingmu--queen-sunduk.scene: INTRODUCING KING MU of Baekje, old and grinning, who has buried a great many Silla plans and keeps the shovel handy. Late afternoon in his palace hall at Sabi, the day the envoys bring the news from Silla. Low three-quarter angle: the old king sprawls sideways on his throne, one elbow on the armrest, a wine cup tilting in his fist, and leans toward the camera mid-laugh with a wicked, delighted grin: "So that old brat Jinpyung is finally dead… Bah! Good riddance." Deep laugh-lines, eyes squeezed narrow and sly, the grey moustache lifted by the grin. Late sun slants through tall lattice doors and rakes across his face and crimson robe in hard amber-gold (#b8862c). Behind him, painted loosely in warm dust and incense haze: red lacquered pillars, a dim folding screen, the soft bokeh of bronze lamps, and at the frame edge the out-of-focus bowed back of a messenger in Baekje court robes.

taizong--queen-sunduk.scene: INTRODUCING THE SECOND EMPEROR of Tang, master of the largest empire under heaven, a man who has never lost a war. Night in his palace hall in Chang'an, the night the news of a woman king arrives. Low three-quarter angle from the floor below the dais: he lounges on a black-lacquer imperial couch, one arm draped over the armrest, chin propped on two fingers, and looks down at a painted scroll of red, white and purple peonies held open at the frame edge by a eunuch's out-of-focus hands in Tang court sleeves. A scornful, amused curl of the lip under the thick beard, one brow cocked: "A woman king… those Samhan barbarians are at it again, aren't they?" Fierce eyes, heavy lazy power in the slouch. Candle flames on a tall bronze stand beside him light him from below in hard amber-gold (#c97a2e). Behind him, painted loosely like a Chinese historical drama at night: vermilion pillars, a white balustrade, incense haze, deep blue-green night beyond the open doors, and many small gold candle-flame bokeh dots, all plain blurred points of light.

alchun--harmony-council.scene: INTRODUCING ALCHUN, Yushin's old yardmate: blunt, folksy, and the only man on the Council who has killed a tiger. The night before the coronation, in the Harmony Council chamber at Seorabeol, where the great lords vote by moving pieces across a cup. Low three-quarter angle across the low council table: he slouches back on his cushion, one big scarred hand rubbing the back of his neck, the other slapped down flat on his knee, nothing in his hands and nothing on the table but one plain bronze cup, and rolls his eyes at the rafters with a long-suffering, folksy grin: "Well. Somebody say something new, or we're here till the frost." A brazier at his side lights him from below in warm orange; the drifting smoke around him is tinted cool steel-blue (#8fb3e0). Behind him, painted loosely: dark timber pillars, a paper lattice window with blue night beyond, brazier smoke curling through the dark, the soft bokeh of oil lamps, a dim robed councillor's shoulder in Silla court silk at the frame edge.

bidam-young--harmony-council.scene: INTRODUCING BIDAM, the youngest sleeve on the Council, who has never once waited his turn. The night before the coronation, in the Harmony Council chamber at Seorabeol. Low three-quarter angle from the floor beside the low council table: he is rising from his cushion mid-sentence, one knee still down, one hand raised palm-out to cut the room off, a string of dark wooden prayer beads looped around that wrist; bright, unafraid eyes and a faint self-amused smile as he speaks over the old men: "My lords have said one word forty times tonight. 'Woman.'" A brazier on the floor beside him lights him from below in hard warm light; the shadows and smoke around him sink into deep navy (#141C2E), and the beads catch small navy-black glints. Behind him, painted loosely: dark timber pillars, brazier smoke curling up through the dark, a paper lattice window with blue night beyond, the soft bokeh of oil lamps, the dim out-of-focus shoulder of an old lord in Silla court silk at the frame edge.

jinheung--jinheung-the-cloud.scene: INTRODUCING KING JINHEUNG, the Cloud King: wherever he rides, the border rides after him. A windswept mountain summit at the edge of land he has just taken, beside a tall rough granite boundary stone, its blank face turned away from us. Worm's-eye angle from the rocks below: he sits his horse on the crest, turned in the saddle to look back over his shoulder at the valleys below with calm, unhurried certainty, one hand on the reins, the other resting on his thigh, the gold Silla crown on his head. The face of a man checking a deed, not making a boast. Behind him a VAST BRIGHT SKY of towering cloud, the clouds he is named for, painted in broad wet strokes of white, slate and blue (#2f6fd4), wind tearing wisps off the ridge, far blue mountain ranges dissolving below. Hard afternoon sun breaking through a gap in the cloud rakes across his face, beard and gold brocade from the side; cloud shadow falls across half his body for contrast.

euija-prince--prince-euija.scene: INTRODUCING PRINCE EUIJA of Baekje, thirty-two, five days from being crown prince, with fifteen sons and an opinion about everything. Afternoon in the rear garden of the palace at Sabi: a pavilion over a lotus pond, a baduk board on a low table. Low three-quarter angle across the board: he sprawls on one elbow on the pavilion floor, holding out a small shallow round bronze wine cup (a low stemless bowl that sits in his palm, no stem, no foot) toward the frame edge without looking, laughing big and loud with his head tipped back, his cynical eyes still sliding sideways to the board: "If I'm to be cheated, I want a professional. Ha! Pour." A slanting afternoon sun through the willows and the pavilion eaves rakes across his face in hard amber-orange (#e08a2e). Behind him, painted loosely in warm green-gold haze: drooping willow, the lotus pond glittering as bokeh, a red pavilion pillar; at the frame edge only a lady's out-of-focus hand and silk sleeve in Baekje court dress, tipping a squat earthenware wine jug toward his cup.

gyebek-boy--prince-euija.scene: INTRODUCING GYEBEK, about thirteen, a river boy with no name until a prince lent him one; he means to pay it back. The palace sand yard by the Baekgang river, the instant the crowd roars the royal surname over him: "Buyeo Gyebek!" Low three-quarter angle from the sand in front of him: a thin barefoot boy in plain undyed white hemp, kneeling on one knee on the chalk-lined sand, his right forearm resting across his raised knee. In that right fist he holds a plain straight wooden practice stick (no guard) in a REVERSE GRIP, the way you hold a dagger to stab downward: the stick runs BACKWARD out of the little-finger side of his fist and lies flat along the outside of his forearm, past his elbow, its tip pointing back behind him; only a thumb's width pokes out above his thumb. Nothing points forward. He turns his head and looks back over his shoulder and UP at the royal seats behind him, his face in three-quarter profile, flat and unblinking, jaw set, saying nothing — a stillness that is already a vow. Low late-afternoon sun from the side rakes across his face and the white hemp in hard yellow-gold (#d9b13a); dust hangs gold in the air. Behind him, painted loosely: the wide river glittering through haze, a high wooden viewing stand under coloured silk awnings dissolving into bokeh, its seated nobles only tiny blurs, pennants stirring in the river wind.

elderyunbi--eight-great-clans.scene: INTRODUCING THE ELDER OF YUNBI, head of the Yunbi house, whose family business is knowing things first. The crown prince's day in the palace yard at Sabi: a square grid chalked on pale sand far below, the young men of the great houses stepping onto it in white. On the high stone viewing steps, low three-quarter angle from one step beneath him: he sits with his hands folded inside his wide sleeves and leans a little toward a rival lord off-frame without turning his head, speaking out of the side of his mouth, eyes sliding sideways, the driest half-smile in the grey beard: "Then keep your boys' wrists honest. The chalk does not care whose sleeve they hold." Bright late-morning sun from the side rakes across his face, his braided grey locks and the red-and-gold robe, with deep shadow inside the sleeves; a sage-green (#7f9b6b) silk awning above throws a cool green tint into the shade. Behind him, painted loosely in sun haze and drifting sand dust: the chalk grid below, tiny white-clad figures dissolving, clan pennants on poles, the river glittering beyond the palace wall.

gyeonggeunchogo--gunchogo-the-13th.scene: INTRODUCING KING GEUNCHOGO of Baekje, the king every later Baekje king quotes when he wants to sound brave. Winter, on the frozen northern road at the head of his army, the walls of Pyongyang finally in sight across the river valley. Worm's-eye angle from the snow beside his horse: he leans forward in the saddle, both gloved hands stacked on the saddle-bow over the reins, breath steaming, and grins at the distant walls with hungry, steady confidence: "Nobody from the south has ever stood on that wall." A heavy dark fur cloak over his crimson robe falls over his hips and thighs, hiding everything at his waist: no sword, no hilt and no weapon in frame; the Baekje king's black cap with its twin gold ornaments on his head. A low winter sun breaks through snow cloud behind his shoulder and rakes across his face and the gold in hard pale gold (#eec052). Behind him, painted loosely in blowing snow and cold blue-grey haze: a frozen river, the long grey line of Pyongyang's walls and a distant gate tower dissolving in mist, a few dark pennants of his host snapping in the wind.

gulgul--commander-yeon.scene: INTRODUCING GULGUL, a Mohe boy of about twelve who will not move out of a burned doorway. Winter, in a Mohe village the Goguryeo Eastern Command has finished with: snow settling on black ash. Worm's-eye angle from the ash at his feet: he stands braced in the doorway of a house that no longer has a roof, gripping a stick like a spear in both fists, its point pressed against the armoured chest of a towering man who is only a dark out-of-focus shape at the frame edge; he glares UP at him, silent, jaw locked, eyes hard and bright, saying nothing at all. Shaved crown with one dark centre strip, two long braids, blood-streaked cheeks, ragged fur over a white wrap, exactly as on the sheet. A low pale winter sun breaks through the smoke behind the ruins and rakes across his face from the side; dull red (#8b3a3a) embers still smoulder in the charred beams around him. Behind him, painted loosely: charred posts, falling snow, grey-blue smoke drifting across a pale winter sky.

dosuryu--commander-yeon.scene: INTRODUCING DOSURYU, an old friend of Yeon's and the one man at the outpost who asks the commander questions. Winter, the burned Mohe village: snow on black ash, just after the commander has put a feral boy on the second horse. Low three-quarter angle: Dosuryu sits his horse a little apart, reins gathered in one gloved hand, the other stroking his long black beard, head tilted, one brow raised in dry, patient doubt as he looks off-frame at his commander: "…You are taking him?" The black pointed cap with two tall feathers and the rust-orange robe with black trim from the sheet, under a dark fur mantle. A low pale sun breaks through the smoke and rakes across his face from the side; where it hits, the falling snow and smoke turn a dusty rose (#c98578). Behind him, painted loosely: charred posts and roofless walls, falling snow, drifting grey smoke, the dark shape of a second horse at the frame edge.

yeontaejo--commander-yeon.scene: INTRODUCING YEON TAEJO, the old Eastern Commander, who sat in the capital's big chair long enough to know what it costs. That first winter, in his house at the eastern command, the day the summons comes. Low three-quarter angle across a low table: the old man sits hunched by a brazier in his fur-trimmed overcoat and leans forward to press the heavy bronze commander's seal (its face turned down) into his son's palm — only a big young hand reaching in from the frame edge — holding on to it a moment too long, tired watchful eyes under the heavy Yeon brows: "Take the seal. You sit in my place this year. …And say half of what you think." Snow-white topknot tied with red cord and long white beard, as on the sheet; no sword and no weapon in frame. The brazier at his knee lights him from below in deep crimson (#8f3a2e) and ember orange. Behind him, painted loosely: dark timber walls, brazier smoke, a paper lattice window glowing pale blue with snowlight, snow falling beyond it as soft bokeh.

gusesa--high-summit.scene: INTRODUCING YEON GUSESA, the High Commander, who chairs the room like a feast and counts it like a granary. The High Summit in the great hall at Pyongyang: the commanders of every front around a long low table of cups and counting sticks. Low three-quarter angle from the far end of the table: he sits at its head in his armour and spreads both open hands over the cups like a genial host calming a dinner quarrel, a mild, patient smile under the beard, the eyes above it cold and calculating: "Each front believes it is the only front. That is why we meet." The ring-pommel hilt of his sword rises over his shoulder from his back. Open bronze oil-dish lamps on tall bronze stands beside the table — bare flames burning in shallow saucers, no glass, no chimney, no cage, nothing hanging from the ceiling — light him from the side in warm brick red (#b2554a), carving the lamellar plates. Behind him, painted loosely: red lacquered pillars, a hanging plain red war banner, lamp smoke and haze, the soft bokeh of more open flames, and at the frame edge the dark out-of-focus shoulder of another commander in Goguryeo armour.

samsin--high-summit.scene: INTRODUCING SAMSIN, the birth goddess, who does not knock. After midnight in a Goguryeo house where a birth is going wrong. On the timber wall hangs an old silk scroll PICTURE of her: a faded painted figure of a white-haired woman in blue and red, images only, with no calligraphy and no characters anywhere on it. She steps OUT of that scroll the way steam steps from a kettle — her trailing sleeve and the hem of her chima still dissolving into curls of painted steam at its edge — and leans down toward the bed below the frame, one hand reaching out, palm down, gentle and grave: "Do not weep. I will open the breath." White hair, gold hair ornament and swirl hairpin, cream jeogori, deep blue and red silk as on the sheet; no glow, no halo, no outline light around her. One small open clay oil-dish lamp on the floor (a shallow saucer with a single wick flame, no glass) lights her from below in warm light, with a soft pink (#e8b4c8) bloom in the steam around her. Behind her, painted loosely: dark timber walls, steam and lamp smoke drifting, the soft bokeh of the one flame; of the bed only a dark quilt edge at the bottom of the frame, nobody visible in it.

gwanggaeto--gwanggaeto-the-great-king.scene: INTRODUCING GWANGGAETO, Goguryeo's widest king; the stele ran out of room before he ran out of fortresses. Dusk at his war camp in the north, the day a Silla envoy brings a letter signed with the word 'servant'. Worm's-eye angle beside his horse: big and imposing in the saddle, in the armour and red cape from the sheet with the Goguryeo gold crown in place of the helmet, he leans down holding the letter rolled shut in one fist and lifts one brow, a slow, dangerous, amused smile in the beard: "Servant. He wrote that word himself?" No weapon in his hands. A low red sunset (#e0442e) rakes across his face, beard and armour plates from the side. Behind him, painted loosely in dust and dusk haze: a wide valley, a herd of cavalry horses and long red banners dissolving into the glow, campfire smoke rising, the first stars in a deep blue sky.

sadaham--sadaham.scene: INTRODUCING SADAHAM, thirteen, the First Class's brightest boy, who makes promises the way other boys throw stones. Night in the new Hwarang dormitory hall at Seorabeol, in the one gap left between bedrolls, which he shares with his new friend. He is a BOY OF THIRTEEN: the sheet's face made younger, a slim narrow-shouldered boyish build, smooth cheeks, no stubble; the crescent-moon headband, long dark hair and light blue robe from the sheet. Low angle from the floor mat: he props himself up on one elbow on his bedroll and jabs a finger across at the friend beside him (only an out-of-focus quilt and a white hemp hanbok sleeve at the frame edge), grinning like a dare, eyes bright with mischief: "You snore. Don't argue. The whole hall heard you." Cold moonlight (#6fa8ff) through a paper lattice window rakes across his face and the rumpled blanket in hard ice-blue. Behind him, painted loosely: dark timber rafters, rows of empty bedrolls dissolving into blue night shadow, dust floating in the moonbeams, and far off on the floor one small open clay oil-dish lamp — a shallow saucer with a single bare wick flame, no glass, no chimney, no metal frame, no handle — as one warm bokeh point. No lanterns anywhere.

mugwan--sadaham.scene: INTRODUCING MUGWAN, thirteen, Sadaham's best friend in the First Class, who says less than his horse. The same night in the new Hwarang dormitory hall at Seorabeol. He is a BOY OF THIRTEEN: the sheet's face made younger, a lanky boyish build, smooth cheeks, no stubble; the crescent-moon headband, long black hair spread on the pillow and the white robe with crimson collar from the sheet. High angle looking down at him from beside his bedroll: he lies flat on his back with his hands folded behind his head and slides his eyes sideways toward the frame edge where his friend lies, perfectly deadpan, the tiniest twitch at one corner of his mouth: "That was you." NOBODY ELSE IS IN FRAME — no second head, no shoulder, no figure in the foreground; at the frame edge only the rumpled, out-of-focus edge of the neighbouring quilt. Cold moonlight (#7aa0c8) through a paper lattice window lays hard blue-grey bars of light across his face and blanket, the rest falling into deep shadow. Around him, painted loosely: dark floorboards, a rumpled quilt, a wooden pillow, moon-dust in the air, and far off on the floor one small open clay oil-dish lamp — a shallow saucer with a single bare wick flame, no glass, no chimney, no lantern — as a faint warm bokeh point.

pumsuk--gotaso.scene: INTRODUCING KIM PUMSUK, rich, handsome, and legal by about an inch. A bright afternoon gyuku match on the field at Seorabeol, the instant he takes the ball with a showy off-side cut. Low three-quarter angle from the turf beside his galloping horse: he leans far out of the saddle with the long gyuku club swung back — five coloured rings on its shaft, presentation silk still on its head — but his face is turned toward the stands and the camera, catching someone's eye half a breath too long, with a cocky, dazzled little smile. The blue crescent-moon headband and light blue robe from the sheet, headband tails streaming in the wind. Hard bright sun from the side rakes across his face and the silk; the sky behind him is a clear vivid blue (#7EB8F0) with torn white cloud. Behind him, painted loosely in flying dust: the trampled field, coloured pennants, other riders as soft dark blurs, the far stands under silk awnings dissolving into bokeh.

chunmyung--pumsuk.scene: INTRODUCING PRINCESS CHUNMYUNG, the Queen's elder sister and Chunchu's mother, who gave up a throne to marry for love. Dusk at her granddaughter Gotaso's wedding in the palace courtyard at Seorabeol: she stands beside the Queen at a doorway the bride has just passed through. Low three-quarter angle: she turns her head toward her sister just off-frame, lips curving in a wry, sad, loving smile, her eyes still on the empty doorway, and answers dryly: "Four. If Your Majesty counts honestly." Long grey hair under the gold hair ornament, purple earrings, the magenta-crimson outer robe over rose and plum silk, exactly as on the sheet. Warm torchlight from the side rakes across her face and the silk, with a soft lilac (#d8a0e8) dusk in the shadows. Behind her, painted loosely: a red-pillared doorway hung with wedding silks, drifting incense, a deep violet dusk sky, small warm lights as soft gold bokeh; at the frame edge only the out-of-focus crimson shoulder of the Queen's court robe.

namseng-heir--academy.scene: INTRODUCING YEON NAMSENG, seven, Yeon's eldest, who would very much like to be told he did well. He is a LITTLE BOY OF SEVEN — the same person as the sheet, but as a small child: the sheet's eyes and brows in a round child's face, NO beard, NO moustache, NO armour, NO sword; a small child's topknot and a plain dark red child's hanbok jacket. Daytime in the family's study room in Pyongyang, at the low table where a monk teaches the sutra. Low three-quarter angle across the table: he kneels bolt upright on his cushion, small hands flat on a closed sutra scroll, and looks UP past the camera toward his father with eager, anxious eyes and a hopeful little half-smile: "I will read the sutra too, if I am allowed." A slanting shaft of winter daylight through a paper lattice window rakes across his face from the side, with a brick-red (#c25a4e) glow off the lacquered table. Behind him, painted loosely: dark timber walls, incense smoke curling in the light shaft, and at the frame edge the out-of-focus grey sleeve of a Korean Buddhist monk's robe.
